documents: Liu et al. 2023, Basin Research 35:489-509, published paper (PDF)

entry.evidence: similar zircon crystallization ages from different source regions greatly hamper the interpretation of sediment dispersal and recycling processes

sequences.source_document: Liu et al. 2023, Basin Research 35:489-509 (published PDF)

steps.action: Pose the problem that recycling and mixed distal and proximal supply make post-orogenic sediment dispersal hard to reconstruct from detrital zircon single U-Pb ages.
steps.quote: impede the reconstruction of post-orogenic sediment-dispersal and recycling processes

steps.action: Design the test by choosing post-orogenic intervals of the Permian Basin and eastern GOM, which are dominated by non-diagnostic Palaeozoic and Grenville grains and already have some core-rim data.
steps.quote: provide the unique opportunity to test the power of using core–rim age pairs on sediment-dispersal interpretation

steps.action: State the conceptual model (Figure 1): distinct rim ages on shared core ages pinpoint source regions, and absent shared core-rim pairs preclude a routing.
steps.quote: if we could not find the same core–rim age pairs in Basin 1 as those in Basin 2, then we can preclude Route C

steps.action: Take from the authors' earlier work the expected rim signatures: 500-300 Ma rims on Grenville cores for the southern Appalachians, 750-500 Ma rims for Gondwanan terranes in Mexico.
steps.quote: Various rim ages in different parts of the Grenville basement distinguish the ubiquitous Grenville DZ component of sedimentary rocks in North America

steps.action: Collect five early post-orogenic samples (four Northern Shelf subsurface, one Eastern Shelf outcrop) and one upper Miocene eastern GOM outcrop sample, with depositional ages from stratigraphy.
steps.quote: We obtained five early post-orogenic samples

steps.action: Date unpolished, randomly mounted zircons by depth-profiling LA-ICP-MS along the C axis (20-30 um spot, about 17 um depth), analysing at least 130 grains per sample, and reduce the data in Iolite with relaxed discordance filters.
steps.quote: U–Pb age data were generated at the UTChron lab at The University of Texas at Austin using depth-profiling LA-ICP-MS

steps.action: Run GJ1 as the primary reference standard every five grains and Plešovice as the secondary standard every 20 grains.
steps.quote: was treated as the primary reference standard and was analysed between every five DZ grains

steps.action: Integrate published core-rim data from the same laboratory and procedure for the Permian Basin, Marathon foldbelt, southern Appalachian foreland and eastern GOM.
steps.quote: These published data were acquired from the same laboratory using the same analytical procedure and data-reduction scheme.

steps.action: Report 1045 concordant ages and 81 core-rim pairs, define age groups A-E, and plot sample KDEs (Figure 5) showing differences between the Northern Shelf, Eastern Shelf and GOM samples.
steps.quote: We obtained 1045 concordant U–Pb ages from 964 DZ grains from 6 samples, and 81 of them (8.4%) have rim ages

steps.action: Plot 58 diagnostic core-rim pairs (Figure 6), group them into Clusters A, B and C, and assign them to Mexican Gondwanan (A, B) or southern Appalachian (C) sources.
steps.quote: Clusters A and B represent typical sources from Gondwanan terranes in Mexico

steps.action: Compile published syn- to post-orogenic single-age data (Figure 7) and show that Group A and C ages cannot discriminate between sources.
steps.quote: Provenance interpretation using single U–Pb ages of zircons from AOM foreland and its vicinity has high uncertainty.

steps.action: Set the rival source regions, the southern Appalachians and the Gondwanan basements in Mexico, for the ubiquitous Palaeozoic and Grenville grains.
steps.quote: both the Appalachians and basements in Mexico could be the potential source regions

steps.action: Compare post-orogenic core-rim assemblages with the synorogenic reference assemblages of each foreland (Figure 8); the Cluster B share falls in the Permian Basin as Cluster C appears.
steps.quote: the proportion of Cluster B grains decreases from 85% to 71% from syn- to post-orogenic stages

steps.action: Infer a mixed Appalachian and Mexican supply to the post-orogenic Northern Shelf, with Appalachian input increasing after the orogeny.
steps.quote: suggests the increasing input of Appalachian sources from syn- to post-orogenic stages

steps.action: Check the Northern Shelf model against published delivery models built from other methods: transcontinental fluvial, aeolian and subaqueous routes via the midcontinent (Figure 9).
steps.quote: The model based on the integration of zircon core–rim age assemblages and single U–Pb ages is consistent with previous sediment-delivery models built by other methods

steps.action: Infer a Mexican Gondwanan source for the Eastern Shelf (12 of 15 Grenville cores with Neoproterozoic rims) and distinct source-to-sink systems on the two shelves.
steps.quote: The dominance of Clusters A and B suggests a diagnosis of Gondwanan terranes of Mexico

steps.action: Check the two-shelf routing against published wireline-log, core-description and single-age models.
steps.quote: Different sediment routing systems acquired from the core and rim ages are consistent with previous models built by other methods.

steps.action: Apply the method to Miocene eastern GOM sand and infer recycling from the southern Appalachian foreland, because its core-rim pairs match the foreland's Cluster C.
steps.quote: suggest that sediments in the Miocene samples were recycled from the southern Appalachian foreland basin and its vicinity

steps.action: Exclude long-shore mixing from the western GOM because 700-500 Ma rims on Grenville cores are scarce.
steps.quote: precludes the possibility of long-shore mixing from the western GOM

steps.action: Check the GOM result against published single U-Pb spectra, zircon (U-Th)/He ages, apatite fission-track data and sedimentological studies.
steps.quote: demonstrate high consistency with results from previous studies using DZ single U–Pb age, DZ (U–Th)/He age, apatite fission track data

steps.action: Bound the method's claim with four limits: looser discordance filters, low rim fertility, no quantification of recycling, and possible abrasion of rims.
steps.quote: However, limitations should also be noted.

steps.action: Keep core-rim age pairs as an exportable extra constraint on provenance and sediment dispersal.
steps.quote: core–rim age pairs provide an extra constraint on provenance interpretation and will have a profound impact on future source-to-sink studies

tree.answer: Recycling and mixed sources make post-orogenic dispersal ambiguous from DZ single ages
No; provenance is inferred from traces (zircon core and rim ages)
Test whether core-rim pairs resolve dispersal and recycling
Southern Appalachian versus Mexican Gondwanan sources; long-shore mixing from the western GOM
Yes: 500-300 Ma versus 750-500 Ma rims on Grenville cores
Found: past strata sampled as traces
Consistent with other-method published models in two regions
Kept: method useful; dispersal models consistent with prior work

end.claim: Detrital zircon core-rim age pairs, measured by depth-profiling LA-ICP-MS, add a diagnostic constraint that separates Appalachian from Mexican Gondwanan sources in post-orogenic strata, giving Permian Basin and eastern GOM dispersal models consistent with other methods, within stated limits.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the depth-profiled core-rim pairs, which reveal the Cluster C (Taconian rims on Grenville cores) signal in the Northern Shelf and eastern GOM samples, neither the method claim nor the dispersal models would exist.

gates.evidence: Action: the regions were chosen to test the core-rim tool under the conceptual model (p. 490-491), but no specific dispersal hypothesis directed sampling. Claim: agreement with published other-method models could have failed, but no failure criterion or statistical test is stated, and the comparisons are qualitative (p. 502-503). Registration: nothing is reported as fixed before the data.

novelty_claims.quote: Detrital zircon core–rim age pairs of Appalachian signals are discovered in the Marathon foreland.
This study demonstrates that this novel strategy, using DZ core and rim ages, will add an extra component
this novel strategy of using core and rim ages could be integrated with other methods

limits: No peer-review file was supplied (a Publons history exists, p. 505), so no review sequence is coded. The checks of the dispersal models compare against results from other methods that are cited, not generated here; the comparison is qualitative, with no statistical test of cluster proportions. Sample sizes of diagnostic grains are small: nine Grenville-core grains with sub-800 Ma rims in the Northern Shelf, five to seven in the GOM, and only four synorogenic pairs in the Marathon foldbelt, which the authors call not robust (p. 501). Sub-claims: the Northern Shelf mixed Appalachian-Mexican supply and the Eastern Shelf Mexican supply are best_explanation; the GOM recycling from the southern Appalachian foreland is best_explanation; the exclusion of western-GOM long-shore mixing is an exclusion resting on the scarcity of 700-500 Ma rims (best_explanation). The method cannot quantify recycling, and rims may be lost to abrasion (p. 504). Inference: the paper does not report whether any data contradicted the prior models, or how its looser discordance filters affect the cluster assignments.

disagreements.target: Common view that Group C (Grenville) grains derive from the southern Appalachians (e.g. Gehrels et al., 2011)
disagreements.support: Cites numerous studies favouring a Mexican Gondwanan source for the Permian and Fort Worth basins, and the decoupling of Group A and C grains.
disagreements.quote: It was commonly thought that Group C grains are derived from the southern Appalachians (e.g. Gehrels et al., 2011).

disagreements.target: View that Group A (500-260 Ma) grains derive from Appalachian Taconian, Acadian and Alleghenian events (e.g. Thomas et al., 2017)
disagreements.support: The same ages occur in Mexican basements, and Group A without Group C in Leonardian strata implies at least partial Mexican derivation.
disagreements.quote: However, these ages are not diagnostic because they could also be sourced from Gondwanan terranes in Mexico

disagreements.target: Provenance practice relying on DZ single U-Pb ages
disagreements.support: Shows that the ubiquitous Group A and C ages have two potential source regions, and that core-rim pairs add discrimination.
disagreements.quote: reveal the weakness of using DZ single U–Pb age to interpret the provenance and sediment dispersal
